slides.title: Everything is numbers
slides.text: Inside a computer, every number, letter and color is stored as bits: switches that are on (1) or off (0).
slides.alt: Pro bits opens with five switches and a bigger ask: make 21, where every place is worth double the last.

slides.title: Binary place values
slides.text: In binary each place is worth double the one to its right: 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. Switches 16, 4 and 1 on read 10101, which is 16 + 4 + 1 = 21.
slides.alt: The switches read 16, 4 and 1 switched on: the number 21 written in bits instead of decimal.

slides.title: More bits, more values
slides.text: One bit shows 2 values. Each extra bit doubles that: 2 bits show 4, 3 bits show 8. Eight bits, a byte, show 256.
slides.alt: Eight switches in a row: a full byte, worth 0 to 255. Only the 128 switch is on, making the middle gray.

slides.title: One thing, many codes
slides.text: The same data can be written many ways. Each way is an encoding. A color can be three numbers too: 255, 0, 0 is pure red.
slides.alt: The color round: a swatch to match with three numbers, because a pixel mixes red, green and blue light.

slides.title: The Spark is whole
slides.text: Gizmo's piece flies home — all four pieces are lit, and Netville is shining again. One step is left: come and see what you have done.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Bits & Pixels and finish all 7 levels. Flip switches to send numbers, letters and gray levels.
